newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair seeks court order to overturn flight ban.
newsitem.headline: Martinair seeks court order to overturn flight ban.

text.p: Dutch airline Martinair said on Thursday it will take Schiphol Airport to court on Friday in a bid to overturn a ban on night flights.
Imposed on August 5, the ban prevents noisier aircraft from taking off between 2300 and 0600 local time in a bid to keep noise levels within legal annual limits.

Martinair is seeking a court order effective from Saturday exempting its Boeing 747 charter flights from the ban, which it says would delay early-morning starts by around an hour, resulting in costly amendments to its flight schedule.
"We totally disagree with this unilaterally-imposed decision by Schiphol," Martinair spokesman Udo Buys said.
"We are hoping for an immediate court ruling or an interim arrangement because of the urgent nature of this case," he said.
Martinair argues Schiphol has ignored that its 747-200 aircraft meets stringent so-called Chapter 3 noise requirements.
The airport also makes no allowance for the fact that when carrying passengers its noise levels are significantly lower.
"This ban was aimed at curbing the noise generated by freight aircraft, but our craft has simply been included in the ban despite that it is carrying passengers," Buys said.

The airline says the ban on early morning starts will disrupt its entire day's schedule, affecting some 3,000 charter passengers daily and exposing it to the risk of damages claims from tour operators.
The summary proceedings are due to be heard on Friday at 1300 local, Buys said.
Schiphol said earlier it had attempted to soften the blow for charter companies by continuing to allow night-time landings of charter flights until October 1.
